new_findings.text: The five obfuscated stance constants are pinned by their DECLARED INTEGER VALUE, not by a HUD-colour fingerprint, and the value proof is strictly stronger. §1t99s0§.as and MCSPlayer.as declare them at IDENTICAL line numbers with IDENTICAL values: 27 -> 0, 29 -> 1, 31 -> 2, 33 -> 3, 35 -> 4, against LIGHT/BALANCED/HEAVY/DUAL/REVERSED. setStanceColor cannot separate them on its own — it emits 2 for BOTH BALANCED and REVERSED and 3 for BOTH HEAVY and DUAL — so any claim resting on colour alone is under-determined. This is the artifact that settles §1t12223s0§ = DUAL and §1t12224s0§ = REVERSED, and it is what killed combat-core/reversed-and-dual-reach. Generalises: for any obfuscated enum with a named android twin, compare the declaration block first.

new_findings.text: The per-stat CAP formulas diverge between builds in four of six rows, and one of them feeds the reach model directly. Positionally aligned, same six handlers in the same order: MAXHP web '10 + (lvl+10)*10' vs android '10 + (lvl+10)*5'; MAXCHI identical in both; MAXAP web '30 + (lvl+10)*5' vs android '20 + (lvl+10)'; ATK/DEF/SPD web '1 + (lvl+10)*3' vs android 'lvl + 10'. At level 8 the SPD cap is 55 on web and 18 on android — a 3x difference in the input to baseSlashLength = 120 + floor((90+5*DAN)*SPD/(20+SPD)). This makes the web level-8 Dan-0 reach ceiling 120 + floor(90*55/75) = 186, not the ~130 an android-capped reading gives.

Any progression or reach row derived from the android caps is wrong for v0.717 by a wide margin.
